Police recruit 257 women constables

cards.what_happened: Sri Lankan police have recruited 257 Women Police Constables to better protect women and children and increase female representation in the service. The recruits entered Nikaweratiya Police College on Monday (23) to begin about six months of basic training. The course covers law, fitness, firearms, disaster management, public relations, leadership, and personality development.
details: The Island reports that 257 Women Police Constables have been recruited by the police to strengthen protection for women and children and raise female representation in the force. The new recruits were admitted to Nikaweratiya Police College on Monday (23) to begin approximately six months of basic police training.

Training will include both theory and practice, covering law, police duties, physical fitness, disaster management, public relations, leadership and personality development, and firearms training. The senior management of the Police College will closely monitor the health and welfare of the trainees throughout the course.

Each recruit will receive the monthly government salary for a Police Constable starting from the date of admission to the college. Police said the goal is to give greater priority to the safety of women and children and to strengthen counselling services that help prevent crime.
cards.why_it_matters: It aims to make women and children safer, increase female representation in the police, and improve counselling to prevent crime.
key_facts: Police recruited 257 Women Police Constables in Sri Lanka.
Recruits joined Nikaweratiya Police College on Monday (23).
Basic training will last approximately six months.

Police College management will monitor trainee health and welfare.

More female officers will strengthen counselling and help prevent crime.
cards.blurb: 257 women join Sri Lanka's police for six months of training to protect women and children.
cards.spoken: Good morning. Sri Lanka's police force has welcomed 257 new women constables. The recruits reported to Nikaweratiya Police College on Monday the twenty third to start about six months of basic training. They will study law, police duties, physical fitness, disaster management, public relations, leadership, and firearms. The college's senior management will keep a close eye on their health and welfare throughout the course. From day one, they will draw the regular monthly salary for a police constable. Police say the move is meant to make women and children safer and to give more women a place in the service. They also hope more female officers will improve counselling and help stop crime before it happens.

Foreign-Flagged Suspected Drug Boat Seized

cards.what_happened: The Sri Lanka Navy caught seven suspects and seized a boat believed to be carrying heroin and crystal methamphetamine (ICE) in international waters south of Dondra. The search went beyond Sri Lanka's Exclusive Economic Zone. The stateless boat and the seven suspects are now being taken ashore.
details: The Sri Lanka Navy caught seven suspects and took control of a boat thought to be carrying heroin and crystal methamphetamine, also called ICE. This happened during a search in international waters south of Dondra, in an area past Sri Lanka's Exclusive Economic Zone. The boat had no nationality, so it was stateless.

The Navy said it ran the operation together with local and foreign intelligence agencies and maritime partners. The stateless boat and the seven suspects are now being escorted to shore. There they will be handed to the Police Narcotic Bureau for more investigations and legal proceedings.

The Navy said closer coordination with regional and international maritime partners and stronger surveillance made the operation work. Its Information Fusion Centre in Colombo pulls together data from modern tools, including satellites, to judge intelligence and sea threats. Joint aerial surveillance with the Sri Lanka Air Force has widened how much ocean it can watch.

This seizure came under the government's 'A Nation United' anti-narcotics campaign, started in October 2025. Under that campaign, the Navy has seized drugs with an estimated street value above Rs. 116 billion. Since January 2026, it has handed over 66 boats, including four foreign vessels, and 379 suspects, including 18 foreign nationals, for legal proceedings over drug smuggling. The Navy said more details about the latest seizure will come later.

cards.whats_next: The boat and seven suspects will be handed to the Police Narcotic Bureau for investigation and legal proceedings, and the Navy will release more details later.
cards.blurb: Sri Lanka's Navy seized a stateless boat carrying heroin and ICE south of Dondra, catching seven suspects in a joint anti-drug operation.
cards.spoken: Now here's a story from the waters off Sri Lanka. The country's Navy has caught seven people and taken charge of a boat they believe was packed with heroin and a powerful drug called crystal methamphetamine, or ICE. This happened far out at sea, south of a place called Dondra, in international waters beyond Sri Lanka's own zone. The Navy says it worked with intelligence teams from here and abroad to pull it off. The boat had no flag or nationality, and it's now being brought to shore, where the seven suspects will be handed to the Police Narcotic Bureau for questioning and possible charges. The Navy says this is part of an anti-drug campaign launched in October 2025, which has already led to seizures worth over a hundred and sixteen billion rupees. More details are said to be coming soon.
